header.running_head: Seeking Allaah's Assistance through the Glorious Qur'aan and Adhkaar

blocks.text:
Another narration states that when Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) felt that it was taking too long for him to conquer Egypt, he wrote to Hadhrat Umar (RA) to ask for reinforcements. Hadhrat Umar (RA) sent four thousand troops, with a commander appointed over every thousand troops. Hadhrat Umar (RA) also wrote to Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) saying:
"I have sent you four thousand troops as reinforcements and appointed a commander for every thousand troops. The commander of every thousand troops is a man who is himself equivalent to a thousand troops; (they are) Zubayr bin Awaam (RA), Miqdaad bin Aswad bin Amr (RA), Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) and Maslamah bin Mukhallad (RA). Remember that you have twelve thousand troops with you and an army of twelve thousand can never be defeated for want of numbers."[^1]
The Letter Hadhrat Umar (RA) Wrote to the Commanders in Shaam in this Regard

Hadhrat Iyaadh Ash'ari reports that he was present during the Battle of Yarmook where there were five commanders over the Muslim army (because the five armies had merged there to fight together); (the five were) Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA), Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan (RA), Hadhrat Shurahbeel bin Hasanah (RA), Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) and Hadhrat Iyaadh (RA) (who is not the one reporting this narration). Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s instruction was that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) should be the commander-in-chief if a battle took place. The army then wrote a letter to Hadhrat Umar (RA), informing him that death was storming towards them (because the enemy outnumbered them) and he should reinforce them with more troops.
Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied to their letter by writing:
"Your letter requesting me for reinforcements has reached me. I shall therefore refer you to one who is a more powerful helper and who has a ready army. He is Allaah. Ask Him for assistance because Muhammad ﷺ was assisted at Badr when his forces were less than yours."[^2]
Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) added, "When this letter reaches you, I want you to fight them without writing back to me." The narrator says, "We then fought them and defeated all of them within a distance of four Farsakh (approximately twelve miles). We also earned a large amount of booty. When we discuss the matter, Hadhrat Iyaadh (RA) proposed that we exchange ten of the enemy prisoners for each one of ours.
Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) then asked for someone to race him. A youngster volunteered saying, 'I would like to, if you don't mind.' The youngster managed to beat Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) and I watched him trail behind on his bare-backed horse with his two locks of hair flying furiously behind him."[^3]
Ibn Abdul Hakam, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.151).
Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.6 Pg.213) and Ibn Katheer in his Tafseer (Vol.1 Pg.400).
